newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour denies split over single currency.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour denies split over single currency.

text.p: Gordon Brown, Labour's economic spokesman, denied that the opposition party's leadership was divided on the issue of Britain's membership of the European Union's planned single currency.

"The idea that the Labour party is divided on this issue is quite ridiculous," Brown told a news conference. He said the party had not changed and would not change its position on monetary union. Labour sees advantages in a single currency but would decide in the national interest whether to join when the time was right, and taking into account the consequences a single currency would have on the economy as a whole.
Brown was being quizzed over remarks made on Sunday by Labour's foreign affairs spokesman, Robin Cook, who said it would be hard for Britain to join a single currency immediately upon launch in 1999.
Brown insisted that Cook had repeated Labour's position that Britain under Labour might or might not join monetary union depending on the circumstances.
"We will make the decision in the right way in the national interest," Brown said.

Speaking at the launch of Labour's biggest ever advertising campaign to proclaim "Enough is Enough" after 17 years of Conservative rule, Brown said Labour would propose new investment measures in the coming days including steps to raise long-term high-technology investment in the British economy.
